Fix a finite ordered simplicial complex $K$, a finite group $G$, a finite abelian group $A$ in additive notation, a left action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$, and a normalized inhomogeneous $3$-cocycle $\beta:G^3\to A$. A background $x=(a,B)$ has flat edge labels $a_{ij}a_{jk}=a_{ik}$ and satisfies $\delta_aB=a^*\beta$, with coefficients at the first vertex. Here $(\delta_a t)_{ij}=\rho_{a_{ij}}t_j-t_i$ for a vertex cochain, $(\delta_a\lambda)_{ijk}=\rho_{a_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}$ for an edge cochain, and $(\delta_aB)_{ijkl}=\rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk}$. The cocycle convention is

$$
D(s,t,r,q):=\rho_s\beta(t,r,q)-\beta(st,r,q)+\beta(s,tr,q)-\beta(s,t,rq)+\beta(s,t,r)=0.
$$

The **background gauge 2-groupoid** $\mathcal B(K)$ has these backgrounds as objects. A $1$-arrow $f:x\to y$ is a raw pair $(g,\lambda)$ of vertex $G$-labels and edge $A$-labels with target $y=(b,C)$ given by

$$
b_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1},\qquad \zeta^g_{ijk}(a)=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(b_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(b_{ij},b_{jk},g_k),\qquad C=\rho_gB+\zeta^g(a)+\delta_b\lambda.
$$

Raw pairs remain distinct even when their induced functions on backgrounds coincide. For fixed $g$ and target edge labels $b$, a $2$-arrow $t:(g,\lambda)\Rightarrow(g,\lambda')$ is a vertex $A$-cochain satisfying $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_b t$. There are no $2$-arrows between different vertex labels $g$. Vertical composition adds vertex cochains; the identity $2$-arrow is zero.

For consecutive $1$-arrows $(g,\lambda):x\to y$ and $(h,\mu):y\to z$, write $a,b,c$ for the successive edge labels. Their composite is $(hg,\nu)$, where

$$
\nu_{ij}=\rho_{h_i}\lambda_{ij}+\mu_{ij}+\tau(h,g;a)_{ij},\qquad \tau(h,g;a)_{ij}=\beta(h_i,g_i,a_{ij})-\beta(h_i,b_{ij},g_j)+\beta(c_{ij},h_j,g_j).
$$

Horizontal composition of $t$ on the first arrow and $s$ on the second is $s+\rho_h t$. Identity $1$-arrows have all vertex labels $e$ and edge labels zero. For three consecutive arrows $g,h,k$, the associator from $((k\circ h)\circ g)$ to $k\circ(h\circ g)$ is the vertex cochain $\sigma_i=\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$. Unit constraints are identity $2$-arrows.

A $2$-groupoid here means these data form a bicategory: each pair of objects has a category of $1$-arrows and $2$-arrows; horizontal composition preserves identities and vertical composition; associators are natural and obey the pentagon; units obey the triangle identity; all $2$-arrows are invertible and every $1$-arrow has a reverse up to invertible $2$-arrows. Finiteness means all three sets of labels are finite. Coherence of the displayed data is a separate theorem.

Write $\pi_0\mathcal B(K)$ for the equivalence classes of objects under $1$-arrows. For an object $x$, let $\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)$ be the group of $2$-isomorphism classes of $1$-automorphisms of $x$, and let $\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)$ be the abelian group of $2$-automorphisms of its identity $1$-arrow. In particular, $\pi_2$ retains vertex cochains with $\delta_a t=0$ rather than discarding them. For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed background $s$ on $L$, the **relative background 2-groupoid** has objects restricting exactly to $s$, $1$-arrows with $g=e$ on vertices of $L$ and $\lambda=0$ on edges of $L$, and $2$-arrows with $t=0$ on vertices of $L$.

For every finite ordered simplicial complex and finite data $(G,A,\rho,\beta)$ in the background gauge $2$-groupoid definition, its displayed operations define a finite $2$-groupoid, including the relative version for every subcomplex and fixed boundary field. Its raw $1$-arrows are not identified by their effects on background objects. For $x=(a,B)$,

$$
\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)=\ker(\delta_a:C^0(K;A)\to C^1(K;A)).
$$

If $S_x$ is the finite set of raw $1$-automorphisms at $x$, each $2$-isomorphism class in $S_x$ has $|\operatorname{im}\delta_a|$ elements, and

$$
|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|=|S_x|/|\operatorname{im}\delta_a|.
$$

The same assertions hold relatively, using vertex and edge cochains vanishing on the subcomplex. On a single vertex, $\pi_1=G$ and $\pi_2=A$, with associator determined by $\beta$.

A **finite groupoid** is a small category in which every morphism is invertible, with finitely many isomorphism classes and a finite automorphism group at every object. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal C)$ for its set of isomorphism classes. Its **groupoid cardinality** is

$$|\mathcal C|:=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For an isomorphism-invariant function $f:\pi_0(\mathcal C)\to\mathbb C$, define

$$\int_{c\in\mathcal C} f(c):=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{f(c)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For finite groupoids $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$, its **homotopy fiber** $\mathcal C_d$ has objects $(c,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}d$ and morphisms $u:(c,\alpha)\to(c',\alpha')$ satisfying $\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha$. Define pullback and pushforward of invariant functions by

$$(p^*g)([c])=g([p(c)]),\qquad (p_!f)([d])=\int_{(c,\alpha)\in\mathcal C_d} f([c]).$$

A span $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ of finite groupoids therefore induces the linear map $b_!a^*$ on invariant functions.

derivations.claim: By [F2], the higher field model and its relative versions are finite $2$-groupoids, so their component sets and both homotopy groups are finite. Every denominator $|\pi_1|$ is a positive integer. By [F3] the same holds for the component and automorphism data of the ordinary model. Thus both displayed sums are finite.

An equivalence arrow has a reverse and associators; conjugation by it identifies the $2$-isomorphism classes of $1$-automorphisms at its endpoints. Whiskering with it and its reverse similarly identifies $2$-automorphisms of the identity arrows; the inverse composites are identified with identities by the specified invertible $2$-arrows. These constructions are inverse on the respective classes, so $|\pi_1|$ and $|\pi_2|$ are constant on each component. The invariant $W_K$ therefore makes the higher summand independent of representative. In the ordinary case this is exactly invariance of automorphism orders under conjugation.

At a point [F2] gives $\pi_1=G$, $\pi_2=A$, hence the higher unit-weight sum is $|A|/|G|$. When all $2$-arrows are identities, $\pi_2$ is trivial and $\pi_1$ is the ordinary automorphism group, so the higher prescription equals the ordinary one.
The finite, representative-independent sums in steps 1.1–1.3 supply the stated ordinary and higher gauging data, including the point normalization and relative prescription.

Let $K$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex. A **finite background field groupoid** $\mathcal F(K)$ is a small category of declared fields and invertible gauge equivalences, with finitely many isomorphism classes and finite automorphism groups. Its automorphisms retain the multiplicities declared by the field model. A **cocycle/action weight** is a function $W_K:\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal F(K)\to U(1)$ constant on every gauge arrow. Its normalized gauging sum is

$$
Z_K(W_K)=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal F(K)}\frac{W_K(x)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F(K)}(x)|}.
$$

For the finite $2$-group specialization, fix finite $(G,A,\rho,\beta)$ and let $\mathcal B(K)$ be the explicit background gauge $2$-groupoid: objects are flat $G$-edge cochains and $A$-face cochains satisfying $\delta_aB=a^*\beta$; $1$-arrows retain raw vertex/edge parameters $(g,\lambda)$, and $2$-arrows are vertex cochains $t$ with $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_{a^g}t$, for fixed $g$. The raw $1$-composition is the displayed $\tau$-corrected composition; its associator is $\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$. Write $\pi_0$ for object equivalence classes, $\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)$ for $2$-isomorphism classes of $1$-automorphisms, and $\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)$ for $2$-automorphisms of the identity $1$-arrow. For a phase weight $W_K$ constant on all $1$-arrows, define the higher normalized gauging sum

$$
Z^{(2)}_K(W_K)=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(K)}W_K(x)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}.
$$

Distinct raw gauge labels are not identified by equality of their effects on fields. The higher sum retains $\pi_2$; it is not ordinary groupoid integration of the $1$-truncation. In particular a point has higher weight $|A|/|G|$ for unit action, whereas an ordinary field groupoid $BG$ has weight $1/|G|$.

For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed field $s$ on $L$, relative fields and arrows use exact restriction to $s$, identity vertex gauge labels on $L$, zero edge gauge labels on $L$, and zero vertex $2$-gauge labels on $L$. Their higher sum uses the same $\pi_2/\pi_1$ prescription. Ordinary groupoids are included as $2$-groupoids with only identity $2$-arrows, so this prescription reduces to the preceding ordinary sum. A higher cocycle supplies an admissible scalar action only after its evaluated weight is proved invariant; nontrivial boundary line-bundle actions require their own transgression data and are not silently treated as scalar functions.

A **finite groupoid** is a small category in which every morphism is invertible, with finitely many isomorphism classes and a finite automorphism group at every object. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal C)$ for its set of isomorphism classes. Its **groupoid cardinality** is

$$|\mathcal C|:=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For an isomorphism-invariant function $f:\pi_0(\mathcal C)\to\mathbb C$, define

$$\int_{c\in\mathcal C} f(c):=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{f(c)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For finite groupoids $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$, its **homotopy fiber** $\mathcal C_d$ has objects $(c,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}d$ and morphisms $u:(c,\alpha)\to(c',\alpha')$ satisfying $\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha$. Define pullback and pushforward of invariant functions by

$$(p^*g)([c])=g([p(c)]),\qquad (p_!f)([d])=\int_{(c,\alpha)\in\mathcal C_d} f([c]).$$

A span $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ of finite groupoids therefore induces the linear map $b_!a^*$ on invariant functions.

Let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be functors of finite groupoids. The **homotopy pullback groupoid** $\mathcal C\times^h_{\mathcal D}\mathcal E$ has objects $(c,e,\alpha)$, where $c\in\mathcal C$, $e\in\mathcal E$, and $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}q(e)$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. A morphism $(u,v):(c,e,\alpha)\to(c',e',\alpha')$ consists of isomorphisms $u:c\to c'$ and $v:e\to e'$ satisfying

$$q(v)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ p(u).$$

Composition is componentwise. The projections to $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal E$ send $(c,e,\alpha)$ to $c$ and $e$, respectively.

derivations.claim: Each $W_i$ is constant on gauge arrows by [F1]. It therefore descends to isomorphism classes, and the finite groupoid integrals defining $Z_K(W)$ and $Z_i(s)$ are finite by [F2].

An equivalence of groupoids induces a bijection on isomorphism classes and an isomorphism on each object's automorphism group. Since $J$ also preserves the weight by the factorization hypothesis, the normalized sum on $\mathcal F$ equals the weighted groupoid cardinality of $\mathcal H$.

Fix representatives $x_2\in\mathcal F_2$ and $x_1\in\mathcal F_1$. The finite set of possible third entries of homotopy-pullback objects represented by this pair is $\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal S}(r_2(x_2),r_1(x_1))$. The group $\operatorname{Aut}(x_2)\times\operatorname{Aut}(x_1)$ acts on it by $(u_2,u_1)\cdot\alpha=r_1(u_1)\circ\alpha\circ r_2(u_2)^{-1}$. Its orbits are exactly the isomorphism classes of triples with this pair of source classes, and the stabilizer of $\alpha$ is the automorphism group of $(x_2,x_1,\alpha)$ by the compatibility equation in [F3].

For a fixed boundary representative $s$, the automorphism group of $(x_i,\eta_i)$ in $(\mathcal F_i)_s$ is the subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F_i}(x_i)$ preserving $\eta_i$. The action of $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F_i}(x_i)$ on the finite set $\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal S}(r_i(x_i),s)$ has these stabilizers. Orbit-stabilizer therefore gives $Z_i(s)=\sum_{[x_i]\in\pi_0(\mathcal F_i)}W_i(x_i)|\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal S}(r_i(x_i),s)|/|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F_i}(x_i)|$.

By orbit-stabilizer, summing the reciprocal stabilizer orders over the orbits in step 1.3 gives $\sum_{[\alpha]}1/|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal H}(x_2,x_1,\alpha)|=|\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal S}(r_2(x_2),r_1(x_1))|/(|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F_2}(x_2)|\,|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F_1}(x_1)|)$. Multiplying by $W_2(x_2)W_1(x_1)$ and summing over $[x_2]$ and $[x_1]$ gives the weighted sum on $\mathcal H$.

Expanding $\sum_{[s]}Z_2(s)Z_1(s)/|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal S}(s)|$ by step 1.4 reduces its coefficient for fixed $[x_2],[x_1]$ to $\sum_{[s]\in\pi_0(\mathcal S)}|\operatorname{Iso}(r_2(x_2),s)|\,|\operatorname{Iso}(r_1(x_1),s)|/|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal S}(s)|$. If the two boundary objects are not isomorphic, every summand is zero. If they are isomorphic, there is exactly one contributing isomorphism class $[s]$; each isomorphism set in the numerator is a torsor for $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal S}(s)$, so the displayed sum equals $|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal S}(s)|$, which is also the cardinality of $\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal S}(r_2(x_2),r_1(x_1))$. This is the coefficient in step 2.1.
Steps 1.2, 2.1, and 3.1 identify the normalized sum on $\mathcal F$ with the stated boundary sum. Step 1.1 proves gauge invariance of every summand and finiteness of all sums.

For each source pair, compatible pullback arrows form the action groupoid of Aut(x2) x Aut(x1) on Iso(r2 x2,r1 x1); orbit-stabilizer gives the stated coefficient. Independently expanded each identity homotopy fiber as Iso(r_i x_i,s)//Aut(x_i); the boundary coefficient is zero for nonisomorphic restrictions and |Aut(s)| for isomorphic restrictions. This proves the formula with 1/|Aut(s)|, including empty fibers/groupoids, trivial stabilizers and finite complex weights. Only finite representative choices, no limiting argument. W invariance, equivalence and factorization are explicit hypotheses; arbitrary boundary cocycles are not inferred. The sole tikzcd square has res2 right, res1 down, and r2/r1 to S, matching the pullback order and stated equivalence; no diagram-dependent proof. Reader/refuter reports found no defect. Freed–Quinn §2/Lemma 2.4 and Moore–Saxena §23.3 (23.34) corroborate weighting; Dijkgraaf–Witten §6.4 gives closed-manifold scope, not the abstract proof.

Thus the groupoid has two isomorphism classes, represented by 1 and s, and each automorphism group is all of C_2.

Give U(1) the trivial G-action. The map chi is a group homomorphism: its values satisfy chi(1)=1 and chi(s)^2=1=chi(s^2). Thus it is a normalized group 1-cocycle. Since conjugation is trivial, W(g)=chi(g) is constant on each arrow and is an admissible action weight.
The normalized sum is $Z(G//G,W)=\chi(1)/2+\chi(s)/2=1/2-1/2=0$.

Here $(\delta_a t)_{ij}=\rho_{a_{ij}}t_j-t_i$ for a vertex cochain, $(\delta_a\lambda)_{ijk}=\rho_{a_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}$ for an edge cochain, and $(\delta_aB)_{ijkl}=\rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk}$. The cocycle convention is

$$
D(s,t,r,q):=\rho_s\beta(t,r,q)-\beta(st,r,q)+\beta(s,tr,q)-\beta(s,t,rq)+\beta(s,t,r)=0.
$$

The **background gauge 2-groupoid** $\mathcal B(K)$ has these backgrounds as objects. A $1$-arrow $f:x\to y$ is a raw pair $(g,\lambda)$ of vertex $G$-labels and edge $A$-labels with target $y=(b,C)$ given by

$$
b_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1},\qquad \zeta^g_{ijk}(a)=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(b_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(b_{ij},b_{jk},g_k),\qquad C=\rho_gB+\zeta^g(a)+\delta_b\lambda.
$$

Raw pairs remain distinct even when their induced functions on backgrounds coincide. For fixed $g$ and target edge labels $b$, a $2$-arrow $t:(g,\lambda)\Rightarrow(g,\lambda')$ is a vertex $A$-cochain satisfying $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_b t$. There are no $2$-arrows between different vertex labels $g$. Vertical composition adds vertex cochains; the identity $2$-arrow is zero.

For consecutive $1$-arrows $(g,\lambda):x\to y$ and $(h,\mu):y\to z$, write $a,b,c$ for the successive edge labels. Their composite is $(hg,\nu)$, where

$$
\nu_{ij}=\rho_{h_i}\lambda_{ij}+\mu_{ij}+\tau(h,g;a)_{ij},\qquad \tau(h,g;a)_{ij}=\beta(h_i,g_i,a_{ij})-\beta(h_i,b_{ij},g_j)+\beta(c_{ij},h_j,g_j).
$$

Horizontal composition of $t$ on the first arrow and $s$ on the second is $s+\rho_h t$. Identity $1$-arrows have all vertex labels $e$ and edge labels zero. For three consecutive arrows $g,h,k$, the associator from $((k\circ h)\circ g)$ to $k\circ(h\circ g)$ is the vertex cochain $\sigma_i=\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$. Unit constraints are identity $2$-arrows.

A $2$-groupoid here means these data form a bicategory: each pair of objects has a category of $1$-arrows and $2$-arrows; horizontal composition preserves identities and vertical composition; associators are natural and obey the pentagon; units obey the triangle identity; all $2$-arrows are invertible and every $1$-arrow has a reverse up to invertible $2$-arrows. Finiteness means all three sets of labels are finite. Coherence of the displayed data is a separate theorem.

For every finite ordered simplicial complex and finite data $(G,A,\rho,\beta)$ in the background gauge $2$-groupoid definition, its displayed operations define a finite $2$-groupoid, including the relative version for every subcomplex and fixed boundary field. Its raw $1$-arrows are not identified by their effects on background objects. For $x=(a,B)$,

$$

$$

$$

Every fixed raw parameter acts bijectively on all background objects: the edge formula determines the original edge labels uniquely and the face formula is affine in $B$ with invertible coefficient $\rho_g$. Local equations identify a field on $K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$ with exactly a pair of fields agreeing on $\Sigma$: each simplex lies in one of the subcomplexes, so assignments glue uniquely and all flatness and tetrahedron equations remain valid. Fix a finite group $G$, finite abelian group $A$, action $\rho$, normalized $3$-cocycle $\beta$, and a finite ordered simplicial complex $K$. Let $\mathcal B(K)$ be the full background gauge $2$-groupoid, retaining its vertex $2$-gauge transformations, and let $W_K:\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)\to U(1)$ be constant on $1$-arrows. Let $V_K,E_K$ be the numbers of vertices and edges and define

$$
c(K)=\frac{|A|^{V_K-E_K}}{|G|^{V_K}}.
$$

Then its higher gauging sum satisfies

$$
Z_K^{(2)}(W_K)=\sum_{[x]}W_K(x)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}=c(K)\sum_{x\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)}W_K(x).
$$

For any subcomplex $L$ and fixed field $s$ on $L$, the higher sum over the relative $2$-groupoid is

$$
Z_{K,L}^{(2)}(s)=\frac{c(K)}{c(L)}\sum_{x|_L=s}W_K(x).
$$

In particular let $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$, where the intersection is the subcomplex $\Sigma$ and all orders are induced. Assume invariant weights $W_i$ and $W_K$ obey $W_K(x)=W_2(x|_{K_2})W_1(x|_{K_1})$. Put $Z_i(s)=Z_{K_i,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)$. These boundary functions are invariant on $1$-arrows of $\mathcal B(\Sigma)$ and obey the actual finite $2$-group gluing law

$$
Z_K^{(2)}(W_K)=\sum_{[s]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(\Sigma)}Z_2(s)Z_1(s)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}.
$$

The empty complex has $c=1$ and one empty field. For a point and unit weight the sum is $|A|/|G|$. When $A$ is trivial these formulas reduce to ordinary finite flat $G$-connection normalization. The theorem assumes scalar invariant weights and their stated factorization; it does not assert that an arbitrary higher cocycle defines such boundary scalar data.

derivations.claim: Normalization is immediate. The cocycle equation expands to $hkl-(g+h)kl+g(h+k)l-gh(k+l)+ghk=0$ since each monomial occurs twice modulo $2$. If $\beta=\delta c$, its values at $(0,1,1)$ and $(1,0,1)$ imply $c(0,0)=c(0,1)=c(1,0)$. Then $(\delta c)(1,1,1)=c(1,0)-c(0,1)=0$, contradicting $\beta(1,1,1)=1$.

Flat edges are determined by three vertex potentials after fixing the potential at $0$, so there are $8$ edge backgrounds. For each, the single tetrahedron equation is one nonzero linear constraint on four face labels, leaving $8$ choices. Thus there are $64$ objects. There are $V=4,E=6$, so $c=2^{4-6}/2^4=1/64$, giving $Z=1$.

Vertex labels first gauge every flat edge assignment to zero: if $a_{ij}=x_i+x_j$, choose $g_i=x_i$. The transformed face field is then an ordinary $2$-cocycle. Set $\lambda_{0j}=0$ and $\lambda_{ij}=-B_{0ij}$ for $0<i<j$; its coboundary is $-B$ on faces containing $0$, and the tetrahedron cocycle equation gives the same on $123$. This gauges every object to the zero background. At zero edges, $\ker\delta$ consists of two constant vertex cochains, so $\pi_2\cong\mathbb Z_2$. Raw automorphisms have constant vertex $G$-labels and an edge $1$-cocycle; these number $2\cdot2^3=16$. The image of $\delta:C^0\to C^1$ has $2^3=8$ elements, so $\pi_1$ has order $2$ and is cyclic.

The one component therefore has higher mass $2/2=1$, agreeing with the object count. The normalized nonzero cocycle remains in the background and associator formulas; no induced-map quotient or replacement by a split model has entered the calculation.

boundaries.evidence: The fixed tetrahedron has four vertices, six edges and four faces; Verification 1.2 counts 8 flat edge assignments times 8 face assignments, giving 64 objects, so its gauging sum has a nonempty index set.
Verification 1.3 gauges each object to the zero background and computes its stabilizers there. This does not set beta to zero: Verification 1.1 proves beta(g,h,k)=ghk is a nonzero cohomology class.
There is one gauge-equivalence component by Verification 1.3, with |pi_1|=|pi_2|=2. Verification 2.1 gives its higher mass 2/2=1, agreeing with 64*(1/64).
Distinct raw automorphisms must not be collapsed by their object action: Verification 1.3 counts 16 raw automorphisms and an 8-element 2-gauge image, leaving pi_1 of order 2 and pi_2 of order 2.

boundaries.reason: The Example is on one fixed ordered tetrahedron, and its 64-object count has no continuous parameter. Vertex order 0<1<2<3 specifies cochain incidence, not endpoints of a limiting interval.

boundaries.evidence: Verification 1.3 fixes the vertex potential at 0, sets lambda_0j=0 and lambda_ij=-B_0ij, giving an explicit gauge to zero for each finite background. No unspecified representative selection is used.

boundaries.reason: The Example proves directly that ghk is a cocycle of nonzero class and computes its single-component higher sum. It does not assert that a higher sum of 1 characterizes nonzero Postnikov class.
The equality Z=1 is obtained from counts and stabilizers after beta is specified; no converse infers beta or the associator from that number.
